content.rationale: .vscodeignore excludes everything it can keep out of the vsix: the repo tooling (.jj/**, .git/**, .deccy/**, .vscode/**, nodes/**, schemas/**, design/**, tests/**, newnode, .gitignore, .vscode-test.mjs, vitest.config.ts, LICENSE), the TypeScript sources (src/**/*.ts, src/data/**, src/graph/**), and node_modules/** wholesale except the two files the extension reads, node_modules/@vscode/codicons/dist/codicon.css and node_modules/@vscode/codicons/dist/codicon.ttf. What the vsix carries is the runtime payload those rules leave in place — out/extension.js, media/webview.html, src/styles/*.css, src/webview/main.js and the two codicon files — plus two packaging metadata files, the manifest package.json and the README. Those two are outside the ignore artifact's control: vsce force-includes the manifest and the README when it builds the vsix whether or not .vscodeignore names them, so the artifact cannot keep them out and does not try to. The README ships as packaging metadata, not as a runtime file; the packaged set is therefore the runtime files plus the manifest and README metadata, not the runtime set alone. Each path the exclude/keep list decides belongs to a prerequisite whose record fixes its place: the development-only suites and runner configurations kuvpymsu and nrwunqtx own leave with the repo tooling, the licence rnqkxwsu records and the repository ignore file rxqsupwm records leave by name, the TypeScript sources srlrwowp's shell and tpztomkv's page entry point are written in leave as sources while the page tpztomkv's composition serves, media/webview.html, is payload no rule may reach, and the manifest srlrwowp owns is force-included metadata the artifact cannot decide.
